headline: Check Tide Charts and Lighthouse Climbing Access
reservation: State park camping is highly competitive and must be reserved through the South Carolina State Parks portal months in advance. Lighthouse climbing requires a separate ticket and may be restricted based on weather or structural maintenance. Verify current entry fees and park capacity alerts on the official Hunting Island site.

days.title: Boneyard Beaches and Lowcountry Tides
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from St. Helena Island

stops.name: North Beach Boneyard
stops.detail: Photograph the weathered, fallen trees along the shoreline, a result of significant coastal erosion.

stops.name: Hunting Island Lighthouse
stops.detail: Climb the historic cast-iron tower for a view of the Atlantic and the ACE Basin.

days.driving: Allow 15-20 minutes from St. Helena; internal park roads are low-speed
days.note: The Boneyard is best explored during low tide; check local NOAA charts.

days.title: Maritime Forests and Marsh Wildlife
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Nature Center

stops.name: Marsh Boardwalk
stops.detail: Walk across the salt marsh to a small hammock island to spot fiddler crabs and wading birds.

stops.name: Lagoon Trail
stops.detail: Look for alligators and herons along the quiet waters of the saltwater lagoon.

days.driving: Minimal driving within the park; allow for walking time between trailheads
days.note: Carry insect repellent for the shaded forest trails, especially in humid months.

days.title: Historic Sea Islands and Beaufort
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from the Park Exit

stops.name: Penn Center
stops.detail: Visit this historic site on St. Helena Island to learn about Gullah-Geechee culture and history.

stops.name: Beaufort Waterfront Park
stops.detail: Conclude with a walk through the historic district to see antebellum architecture and live oaks.

days.driving: Allow 30-40 minutes to reach Beaufort; traffic can slow on the bridge
days.note: Penn Center hours vary; check their official schedule for museum access.

intel.title: Beach Access Lots
intel.text: Parking at North Beach fills rapidly during summer weekends. Arrive early or use the south end lots and be prepared for a longer walk to the boneyard.

intel.title: Coastal Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular reception is generally available but can be spotty under the dense maritime forest canopy. Do not rely on streaming for navigation inside the park.

intel.title: St. Helena Service Hub
intel.text: Fuel and groceries are available on St. Helena Island before you cross the final bridge. No fuel is sold within the state park boundaries.

intel.title: Tidal Planning
intel.text: High tide can significantly narrow the beach and make the boneyard inaccessible. Plan your shore walks around the daily tide cycle for safety and views.

intel.title: Lighthouse Restrictions
intel.text: Children must meet a height requirement to climb the lighthouse. The structure may close during high winds or thunderstorms for safety.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Hilton Head Airport (HHH) and drive 87 minutes via Highway 21, stopping in Lady's Island or St. Helena for supplies before park entry.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are sufficient; campers should check the state park website for specific pad lengths and turn-around limits in the maritime forest.
plan.goldenHour: The Fishing Pier offers an unobstructed view for sunrise, though seasonal gate opening times should be confirmed locally.
